ledger.note: 6000 BCE: the first farmers of the Balkans, the Starcevo-Koros-Cris villages, hold the Danube and Tisza plains. Infobox "circa 6,200 B.C.E."; the Hungarian plain "had been occupied by the Starčevo-Körös-Criş culture" from "as early as 6100 BC" (LBK page); the culture began before the project's first year.

ledger.note: 5400 BCE: the Vinča culture takes the Morava-Danube core. Infobox "Followed by: Vinča culture"; the Vinča page: "dated to the period 5400-4500 BC", "Preceded by: Starčevo culture". The year is the Vinča page's.

region.text: the Koros group of the Hungarian plain, "named after the river Koros in eastern Hungary and western Romania"

ledger.note: 5300 BCE: the Koros group ends and the Alföld Linear Pottery takes the Hungarian plain. Koros "survived from about 5800 to 5300 BC"; the LBK page dates the Alföld culture "At around 5330 BC" to "until about 4940".

5300 BCE: the last Starcevo-Koros-Cris land on the map, the north-west Balkans, goes to nobody. The page ends Koros at 5300 BC but Starcevo "between c. 5500 and 4500 BCE" (or 6200-5200 BCE); no page places the late Starcevo, so the dossier ends with Koros and notes the 4500 BC alternative.

certainty.note: An archaeological culture: radii around the type regions, never a frontier.

sources.note: Dates 6200-4500 BCE, the three regional groups and their countries, the Banat and Transylvania, the Vinča and LBK succession.

notes: Culture dossier, one page. Disagreement: the infobox end (4500 BCE) and the Starcevo range (5500-4500 or 6200-5200 BCE) against the Koros end (5300 BC) and the Vinča start (5400 BC); the dossier ends at 5300 BCE when its land has passed to the Vinča and the LBK, so the late Starcevo of 5300-4500 BCE is not drawn (gap, page silent on where). Lepenski Vir, Karanovo, Sesklo are not described on the page. Gazetteer: Starcevo, Tumba Madzari are not places; Belgrade, Szeged, Timișoara, Deva, Skopje and Tuzla radii stand in; "Banat" and "Alföld" are not regions.
